title: Advanced Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning Models: Enhancing Financial Transaction Security
authors: Fariha, N.; Khan, M. N. M.; Hossain, M. I.; Reza, S. A.; Bortty, J. C.; Sultana, K. S.; Jawad, M. S. I.; Safat, S.; Ahad, M. A.; Begum, M.
venue: International Journal of Accounting and Economics Studies
tldr: Unsupervised ML framework combining Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and deep autoencoder detects approximately 1-2% of credit card transactions as anomalies for fraud surveillance.
problem_and_motivation: The rise of digital payments has accelerated the need for intelligent and scalable systems to detect financial fraud, particularly credit card transaction anomalies.
approach: End-to-end feature-rich ML framework for detecting credit card transaction anomalies using real-world data.
Merges transactional, cardholder, merchant, and merchant category datasets from relational database.
Feature engineering extracts behavioral signals: average spending, deviation patterns, timing irregularities.
Trains unsupervised models: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and deep autoencoder.
Proposes composite risk score aggregating binary flags from all anomaly detectors.
Further segments using K-Means clustering and DBSCAN.
findings: num: Framework detects approximately 1-2% of transactions as anomalies.
Deep autoencoder effectively flags top 1% of reconstruction errors as outliers.
PCA visualizations show effective anomaly separation in latent space.
Composite risk score effectively highlights riskiest cardholders and merchants.

definitions.definition: Unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm isolating anomalies through random partitioning.
Aggregated score from multiple anomaly detectors for prioritizing investigation.

topics.name: Anomaly Detection in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: Core focus on detecting fraudulent credit card transactions as anomalies.

topics.name: Anomaly Detection Algorithms for Personal Spending Data
topics.justification: Implements and compares Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and autoencoder algorithms.

topics.name: Data Privacy and Security in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: Directly addresses financial transaction security and fraud prevention.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a comprehensive unsupervised ML framework for credit card fraud detection combining multiple anomaly detection algorithms. The composite risk score approach offers practical prioritization for fraud investigation.
directly_justifies: Unsupervised models effectively detect 1-2% of transactions as anomalies.
Composite risk score from multiple detectors improves fraud identification.
limits: Unsupervised approach may not detect all fraud types.
Real-world deployment considerations not fully addressed.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 8.A, 8.B, 10.A (high). Rejected Philippine-specific, budgeting, and engagement topics.

limitations: Unsupervised approach may miss known fraud patterns that supervised methods would catch.
Real-time deployment considerations not fully explored. [unacknowledged]
remember_this: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM, and autoencoder detect 1-2% anomalies.
Composite risk score prioritizes high-risk cardholders and merchants.
Unsupervised approach suitable for evolving fraud patterns.
